purpose.is: Owns the one list of every state path the design names and the one script that deletes any of them, so that "keep all artifacts out of the git repo ... ensure we have cleanup scripts for that shit available too" (owner, C35) is a registry the system runs, not a README someone reads.

Runs cleanup on three triggers: a merge (branch gone on the forge, worktree and slot released, the ticket's seat workspaces removed), a backup (retention of older snapshots), and a timer (every registered path by its retention), plus the one-time dispositions of N-49 and N-50.
purpose.is-not: It never decides what is junk by looking; it deletes only what a registry entry or a disposition record names, after a dry-run listing that is itself a record.
purpose.why: 88 registered worktrees, 34 remote branches and 5,812 untracked event copies accumulated because cleanup was a hand step nobody owned (04-UNLANDED.md sections 3, 6, 7; L05 section 5 item 7). merge.sh deletes its branch (merge.sh line 306) but nothing calls merge.sh (L05 section 5 item 11).

input.record: The merge record (PR number, branch, merge sha, ticket id). Trigger class merge.

The backup record exactly as N-05 writes it (record.schema.json#/$defs/input refs ../N-05/record.schema.json#/$defs/backup): path, checksum, retention_class tick, daily, monthly or manual, verified. Trigger class backup.
The daily tick and the hourly tick; the registry says which entries run on which. Trigger class timer.
One per 04-UNLANDED entry with action supersede or close (and land after its ticket merges). Trigger class disposition.
Cancel records name no paths. Trigger class disposition.
branch.delete names the design branch. Trigger class disposition.

output.record: Phase plan: the dry-run listing (every path or ref that would go, its registry entry, its size, its lease state), the plan hash, nothing deleted.
Phase apply: what was deleted, what was skipped and why (lease held, not matching the plan, missing already), the plan hash it executed.
Apply refused: a drain lease is no longer current (reason lease_not_current) or a bound inode changed since the plan (reason plan-changed); nothing further is deleted; the next trigger re-plans.

Three attempts failed on at least one entry; the failed entries and the last error; N-28 posts one card only when the failed entry is in the owner-acts set of the registry (a path only the owner can remove).

registry.s: The registry is generated, like dag.md: rebuild/design/bin/registry.py reads every state-paths element of every node volume and every runbook volume under rebuild/design/nodes and writes rebuild/design/shared/cleanup-registry.json (committed, generated, checked for drift by N-46).

One entry per path (shared/cleanup-registry.schema.json): id (the path's id attribute, or node plus a slug of the glob), node, glob, class (host: a path on the host under an allowed root; store: rows N-45 prunes by the kind's retention class; client: the owner's browser storage; external: another system's retention such as the journal, Jenkins, GHCR or GitHub; tracked: a file in a repository, removed by pull request), retention (an ISO 8601 duration, never, or the run command's rule), trigger (timer, merge, backup, disposition, owner), acts (system or owner), run (the command the volume names; per-group scripts are allowed) and verb, which is always line/bin/cleanup.sh --entry <id>: the one verb the service runs, which looks the entry up and runs its command in plan, then apply, mode.

Retention never with acts owner is the class for a path kept on purpose: long-lived secrets (STATE/config/service.env, $COQ_STATE/secrets/*), the owner's data (the art reference copy, the unlanded backups), records another system keeps (GitHub statuses), the owner's browser storage and tracked sources; cleanup.sh lists such an entry in every plan and refuses to apply it, and only the owner removes it, by break glass or a disposition (registry.py rule R2 and R3; brief C rule 6).

Owner-acted entries (review NF-E4): an entry whose cleanup is break glass, a retirement, an uninstall or disable, a branch protection change, a namespace delete, a token or the store database itself carries trigger owner and acts owner. The service never selects it on a timer, merge or backup trigger and never applies it; cleanup.sh runs it only from the owner CLI under an owner principal (shared/authority.xml#principals), plan then apply, and the run is recorded as a hand line operation (N-51 row A3). registry.py fails the book (rules R7, R8) when such an entry is marked timer or system, and every path must declare trigger and acts explicitly: nothing defaults to timer.

A volume that names a state path with no cleanup and no declared retention never fails N-46 (check.sh C14: every state path the design names has a cleanup script or is declared kept on purpose, brief rule 6).

Git objects are entries too: remote branches (glob refs/remotes/origin/feat/*, trigger merge, retention P0D), local worktrees (the treehouse pool and $COQ_CACHE/worktrees, trigger merge), stale remotes (trigger disposition).

mechanism.where: Go package cleanup in the service decides when; line/bin/cleanup.sh does the deleting as an Executor.Run verb (scheduler.proto line 19) with a timeout; the script lives in the repository (owner 2026-10-12, scripts live in the project).
mechanism.step: On a trigger record, select the registry entries whose trigger class matches and whose retention has elapsed (timer), or whose key matches the record (merge: ticket id and branch; backup: retention class; disposition: the entry or ref the record names).

Take the lease cleanup:<entry-id> for each selected entry (maintenance class, shared/contracts.xml#lease-machine; ttl lease.ttl_seconds). An entry whose lease is held is skipped with reason lease-held and tried on the next trigger.

Drain (review F24): for every resource the entry would touch (a workspace slot, a worktree, a tier page directory, a snapshot, a branch), take the system lease drain:<resource> in one Commit whose preconditions say no live holder lease (workspace:, seat:, tier:, backup:) exists for that resource. Allocators refuse a resource with a live drain lease: N-14 never provisions into a drained slot, N-48 never promotes into a drained tier directory, N-05 never writes a drained snapshot path. A resource whose holder lease is live is skipped lease-held; no drain is taken for it.

Run cleanup.sh plan --entry <ids> --trigger <record id>: it expands globs by a no-symlink walk (every component opened with O_NOFOLLOW from the allowed root's directory descriptor; a symlink anywhere, or a mount point crossed, is refused 400 outside-root), and binds each path to its device, inode, type, size and mtime. The listing, the bindings and the drain lease keys, tokens and generations hash to the plan hash. The service writes cleanup.run 100 with the listing and its hash.

Run cleanup.sh apply --plan <hash>: before any deletion the service re-reads every drain lease of the plan; a lease that is not current (expired, revoked, or a new generation) refuses the apply with cleanup.run 412 lease_not_current. The script walks again from the root descriptors, compares each binding, and refuses with 412 plan-changed when a device, inode or type differs or a path appeared; nothing is re-resolved by string. It then unlinks relative to the verified directory descriptors (unlinkat, depth first; never rm -rf on a path string), removes worktrees with git worktree remove then prune, deletes remote branches with git push origin --delete through the service's forge-pr credential after checking the ref still points at the planned sha, git branch -D for local branches, git remote remove for stale remotes, and treehouse return for pool slots. Each deletion is one row in the result.
Write cleanup.run 200 with the rows; release the drain and cleanup leases in the same Commit. On any failure retry the failed entries only, up to 3, then cleanup.run 423.
mechanism.merge-trigger-detail: For a merge record: delete the remote branch (the repository setting delete_branch_on_merge is set true by N-49 step 5, so this is a check, not a delete, once that lands), remove the ticket's worktrees and seat workspaces (after N-15 has written seat.result for every run of the ticket; a running seat holds a lease and is skipped), return the slot, remove the dev and uat tier pages of the ticket (N-48 registers them).
mechanism.backup-trigger-detail: Retention per class is N-05's (nodes/N-05/spec.xml#output, config backup.retention): tick, daily and monthly snapshots past their class retention are pruned through N-05's cleanup-backups.sh entry, selected from the backups table rows (class, epoch, high_water_seq, row_count, min_retained_seq; shared/state-store.xml, shared/contracts.xml#restore), never by file age; never the newest verified backup of any class; a backup whose record does not carry verified true is never selected. Class manual is owner-acted: kept until the owner's cleanup card, never timer-run.

diagram.mermaid: sequenceDiagram participant T as trigger record participant S as Go cleanup package participant L as N-02 leases participant X as cleanup.sh (Executor.Run) participant R as N-01 store T->>S: merge / backup / tick / disposition S->>L: lease cleanup:<entry> S->>L: drain:<resource> (no live holder lease) S->>X: plan --entry ids (no-symlink walk) X-->>S: listing + inode bindings + hash S->>R: cleanup.run 100 (plan) S->>L: recheck drain leases current S->>X: apply --plan hash (rebind, unlinkat) X-->>S: rows (deleted, skipped, failed) S->>R: cleanup.run 200, 412 or 423 S->>L: release drain and cleanup

safety.rule: Allowed roots only: $COQ_STATE, $COQ_CACHE, the treehouse pool root from treehouse.toml, $HOME/.bearings for tier pages, $HOME/.config/systemd/user and $HOME/.local/bin for the entries that live there (coq unit files and pinned binaries; those entries are owner-acted when they uninstall or disable), and git refs by name. A path outside them, a symlink on the way, or a crossed mount point is refused 400 and the entry is reported as a registry defect.

Atomic exclusion: a resource is deleted only under its own drain lease, taken when no holder lease is live, and every allocator refuses a drained resource; the delete re-verifies the lease generation and the bound inode first (mechanism steps 3 to 5).
Owner-acted entries (trigger owner) never run from a trigger record; the service only lists them.

Never the repository working tree of the owner checkout, never origin/main, never a branch with an open PR unless a disposition record names it, never a worktree whose lease is live, never the stable tier page directory, never the backup newest snapshot.
Plan before apply, always; apply refuses a plan older than cleanup.plan_ttl (PT1H), whose drain leases are not current (412 lease_not_current) or whose bindings changed (412 plan-changed).
Every deletion of a git ref records the sha it pointed at in the result row, so a wrong deletion is recoverable from the reflog or the row for 30 days (N-05 backs up the mirror).
Dry-run output for a disposition run is attached to the owner's card before GOFACTORY (N-49, D25 A); the apply waits for the GOFACTORY ruling record.

start.s: Triggers are records; the service selects entries and runs the script. The daily tick at 02:00Z runs timer entries; the hourly tick runs entries with retention under one day.
No agent runs cleanup.sh in the line; the script is also runnable by hand for the owner's break glass with the same plan-then-apply contract.

wait.fallback: skip the entry or resource this run with reason lease-held; next trigger retries; an expired lease is swept by N-02 (shared/contracts.xml#lease-machine)
kill, count one attempt; after 3 cleanup.run 423 naming the entry
kill; rows already written are kept; the remaining entries retry; an apply killed mid-row leaves a path half-deleted, which the next plan lists again (idempotent)
retry by the N-04 ladder 10, 30, 90 s; then 423; the branch stays and the next merge trigger retries

wait.what: a running seat holding a workspace
wait.timeout: until seat.result (N-15 stall timer bounds it)
wait.fallback: the entry is skipped, never killed by cleanup; N-12 kills stalls

waits.cog-test: The cog that could stall this node is a human deciding what is safe to delete. The registry and the disposition records decide; the dry run makes the decision visible; the lease check makes it safe.

retries.policy: Per failed entry, not per run; entries that succeeded are not re-run.
retries.recover: After the third failure the run ends with cleanup.run 423 naming the entries; the next trigger of the same class plans them again, so nothing is lost and nothing loops within a run.
retries.report: A 423 on a system-acts entry is an alert record (N-41) and a counter; a 423 on an owner-acts entry is one card (N-28) with the dry-run rows attached.

many-agents.readers: Any seat may read the registry volume to learn where its artifacts go; every seat writes only under the paths its node registers.
many-agents.writers: Only the service runs apply. Two triggers selecting the same entry at once (a merge and the hourly tick) are serialized by the per-entry lease; the loser skips with lease-held and the record shows it.
many-agents.collision: A seat starts on a ticket while the merge-trigger cleanup of a previous attempt runs: the new workspace is a new path (attempt in the name) and holds its own lease; the old attempt's path is the one deleted.
Cleanup and N-05 backup on the same snapshot directory: the backup holds lease backup:<snapshot> while writing; cleanup skips it; the newest snapshot is never selected.
Two applies with the same plan hash (a retry after an unknown outcome): the second finds the paths gone and writes rows with reason already-gone; no error.

N-14 allocates a slot while cleanup drains it: the drain Commit's precondition and N-14's provision Commit both touch the slot's lease row; one commits first; the other sees the lease and refuses (cleanup skips lease-held, or N-14 refuses the drained slot and picks another).
A symlink swapped in after the plan: apply walks with O_NOFOLLOW from the root descriptor and compares inodes, so the swap is 412 plan-changed and nothing outside the root is touched.
A disposition record from N-49 and a merge trigger naming the same branch: both plan it; the first apply deletes; the second records already-gone.

status-codes.emits: Plan written; system acts (apply follows unless the trigger is a pre-GOFACTORY disposition dry run).
Drain lease not current, or bound inodes changed, before apply; system acts (replan next trigger).
A registry entry names a path outside an allowed root; system acts (fix ticket request for the volume that registered it).
Three attempts failed; system acts on system entries (alert), owner acts on owner entries (one card).

state-paths.path: Every plan listing by hash (the record holds it too; this is the file the script reads at apply).
The registry as read at a main sha.
state-paths.rule: cleanup.sh --entry N-45.* is the one entry cleanup never selects while a run is in progress (self-cleaning only on the timer trigger when no lease cleanup:* is live).

edges.out: None drawn: cleanup.run is a sink; N-28 and N-41 read 423 by code, N-40 counts.

may.do: plan and apply any registry entry; take cleanup leases; delete refs through the service's forge auth
run cleanup.sh plan and apply by hand as break glass, recorded by N-42; the only actor for entries of trigger owner

may-not.do: run cleanup.sh apply; delete any path it did not create in its own workspace; delete branches or worktrees
delete outside the allowed roots; follow a symlink; delete origin/main; delete the stable tier page; delete the newest backup; apply an entry of trigger owner

monitoring.counter: Entries in 423 state; an alert record when greater than 0 for 24 hours.
From git worktree list on the mirror and the pool; the Stats screen shows it beside the 88 of 2026-10-14 as the baseline.

runbook.step: Read the row's error; if it is a permission or mount problem, fix the host and the next trigger retries; if it is a registry defect (bad glob), the fix ticket request is already cut.
Answer the card; the owner removes the path or rules it kept (a ruling record adds an exclusion to the registry through a ticket).
line/bin/cleanup.sh plan --entry <id> then apply --plan <hash>; both write records; both refuse without the state root set.
The result row holds the sha of a deleted ref; git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<name> restores it from the mirror backup; a deleted state path is restored from the N-05 backup of that day.
runbook.cleanup: Every path in this volume's state-paths element, through this node's own script.
